applies_to: All relevant UI01–UI32 states; evaluate applicability explicitly, never silently skip

cases.title: Light/dark parity
cases.given: each screen and modal in both themes
cases.when: all primary and failure states are exercised
cases.then: the same actions, information and focus behavior work in both; charts/status use text alternatives

cases.title: No first-paint theme flash
cases.given: a saved explicit theme or System preference
cases.then: the resolved theme is applied before content paint; unavailable persistence does not prevent a current-session choice

cases.title: Original-source color fidelity
cases.given: a slide, microscopy image or color-coded graph
cases.then: the underlying source colors/content are unchanged; a separate readable rendition is clearly labeled

cases.title: Accessible names and controls
cases.given: the screen is used with keyboard and assistive technology
cases.when: controls, tabs and dialogs are navigated
cases.then: names/roles/state are exposed, native semantics are preferred, and active tabs/panels have clear relationships

cases.title: Focus and modal recovery
cases.given: a source/correction dialog was opened from a control
cases.then: focus returns predictably; no focus trap, hidden focused control or unsolicited focus transfer occurs

cases.title: Reflow and enlargement
cases.given: app UI text is enlarged to 200% or constrained to a narrow viewport
cases.then: app text and controls remain usable; intrinsically two-dimensional slides use contained zoom/pan plus alternatives rather than shrinking all UI

cases.title: Contrast and non-color status
cases.given: normal/large text and essential controls in each theme
cases.then: normal text target is at least 4.5:1, large text 3:1, essential nontext control indicators 3:1 where applicable; state is not color-only

cases.title: Targets and non-drag alternatives
cases.given: phone, keyboard or limited pointer precision
cases.when: a timeline, range editor, tree or card control is used
cases.then: primary touch controls target 44 CSS px as a product preference, WCAG 2.2 AA 24px-or-spacing exceptions are assessed, and dragging is not the sole action

cases.title: Reduced motion
cases.given: OS or app requests reduced motion
cases.then: nonessential transforms, smooth scrolling and decorative motion are removed while essential meaning remains; no autoplay animations claim progress

cases.title: Media access and truthful alternatives
cases.given: audio/video and slides are available
cases.then: provided alternatives are actually usable and their verification gaps explicit; a text field or generated description alone is not accessibility certification

cases.title: Input before inference
cases.given: an explicit learner answer with attachments
cases.then: verified input is retained with its known durability and no unsupported assessment is claimed

cases.title: No assessment by attendance
cases.given: a learner views a slide, watches a recording or receives a quick answer
cases.then: no new performance event is inferred; existing evidence is neither erased nor downgraded

cases.title: No answer leakage
cases.given: a practice condition excludes solution content
cases.when: search, previews, downloadable payloads or related cards are opened
cases.then: the app-provided context does not leak solutions; unrelated native history cannot be certified as absent

cases.title: Safe content rendering
cases.given: untrusted source/AI text includes HTML, links or instructions
cases.then: text is safely rendered, links remain explicit, and content cannot change grants, execute commands or invoke writes

cases.title: Separate durability stages
cases.given: a draft is local, a bundle in transit, or a response committed
cases.then: labels reflect local persistence, PC acknowledgement, native completion and canonical publication separately; no blanket Saved tick

cases.title: Duplicate admission/publication
cases.given: same request or review event arrives repeatedly
cases.then: one accepted logical response/event exists; same ID with different bytes becomes a visible conflict

cases.title: Cancellation races
cases.given: cancel or supersession occurs near completion
cases.then: current accepted generation is not replaced and an already committed record is not silently erased

cases.title: Current-versus-historical evidence
cases.given: source/rubric changes after an attempt
cases.when: history and current views are opened
cases.then: old evidence retains its original references; affected derived outputs are stale/rebuilt without automatic regrading

cases.title: Time semantics
cases.given: device clocks differ or occurrence time is unknown
cases.then: received/recorded/occurred times and timezone basis remain distinguishable; chronology is not fabricated from sync arrival

cases.title: No evidence in addresses or analytics
cases.given: private navigation and errors
cases.then: routes avoid full answers, tokens and expiring signed URLs; optional telemetry is not enabled by this design

cases.title: Cross-device state integrity
cases.given: two authorized devices update view or drafts
cases.then: explicit source/lineage and per-device preferences govern; no blind last-write-wins over submitted evidence

cases.title: No duplicate ownership
cases.given: new material, canonical save or gap display
cases.then: source registration uses the existing updater, learning uses its own writer, and gap/tree exports remain projections

cases.title: Consumer-visible completion
cases.given: a result manifest arrives before payloads
cases.then: it waits for complete matching bytes or shows the last verified snapshot; local PC publication is not remote delivery proof

cases.title: Reuse without plugin proliferation
cases.given: implementation selects UI dependencies
cases.then: maintained primitives/native capabilities are evaluated before custom code; no library installs, proprietary services or auto agent APIs are implied by the spec
